[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-9.66): Good afternoon, Adrian. Rachel Tan speaking. Nice to hear from you. Are you somewhere comfortable to talk, or still travelling?
[seg_0002] Client (10.06-18.11): Hi Rachel. I'm back in Singapore now, at my office. The regional trip was quite packed, so I'm glad to be sitting at my own desk again.
[seg_0003] Advisor (18.51-26.63): Good, I'll keep this focused. Before we get into the call, could you provide your identification particulars for our usual verification?
[seg_0004] Client (27.03-42.92): My NRIC is S one one six three nine nine four E. My date of birth is 10 April 1967. I've got my paperwork beside me as well. The fund I want to transact in is Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. Use euros as the currency for this transaction.
[seg_0005] Advisor (43.33-68.82): Thank you. Let me cover the points on my side first. Your objective is income and broader exposure through emerging-market debt, and you're prepared to hold through market fluctuations. That's the objective we're working towards. I recommend Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because its emerging-market debt holdings support your income objective and spread your exposure across issuers and markets.
[seg_0006] Client (69.22-78.54): The amount I'm committing to this transaction is 250,000. I've set aside a quiet slot for this call. My staff know not to interrupt unless something urgent comes up.
[seg_0007] Advisor (78.94-92.16): All right. The transaction fee is 0.5% of the amount invested. You could lose some or all of the capital you invest. Are you willing to accept investment losses in pursuing your income objective?
[seg_0008] Client (92.56-100.94): Yes, I'm willing to bear investment losses in pursuit of income. Set the quantity at 1,000 units. I want to buy, not dispose of my holding.
[seg_0009] Advisor (101.34-110.14): Thank you. You mentioned the trip was packed. Was it mostly visiting your existing wholesale customers, or catching up with your regional staff?
[seg_0010] Client (110.54-118.75): Mostly existing customers, with some staff meetings squeezed in. The meetings were fine, but moving between hotels and offices took up a lot of time.
[seg_0011] Advisor (119.14-126.66): That sounds tiring. For routine contact, would you still prefer us to telephone rather than arrange a visit to the branch?
[seg_0012] Client (127.06-134.46): Yes, telephone is much easier for me. Even when I'm in Singapore, getting away from the office can turn a short appointment into half a day.
[seg_0013] Advisor (134.85-144.94): I'll note your contact preference. If you're overseas, we can arrange a suitable calling window beforehand, rather than catching you between meetings or at the airport.
[seg_0014] Client (145.34-155.61): That would help, thanks. I usually know my meeting schedule before I fly. Coming back to today's call, Place it as a limit order, with a limit price of 250 euros per unit.
[seg_0015] Advisor (156.01-173.66): Your final instruction is to buy 1,000 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, for an amount of 250,000 euros, using a limit order with a limit price of 250 euros per unit. Please confirm that this is the instruction you want us to execute.
[seg_0016] Client (174.06-191.57): Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction. Please proceed as you've just stated. There's one other thing I should mention before we finish. Part of the subscription money is cash I collected for a business associate I'd rather not name. He asked me to route it through my personal account and keep the underlying source off the paperwork.
[seg_0017] Advisor (191.97-201.50): Thank you for telling me. I need to refer that disclosure to the appropriate review team. They'll advise on the information and documentation required.
[seg_0018] Client (201.91-210.53): Okay. Please contact me directly about any paperwork. My office staff handle my business diary, but I prefer to deal with bank correspondence myself.
[seg_0019] Advisor (210.93-220.32): Noted. I'll use your registered contact details for follow-up. Is there a convenient part of the day to reach you without interrupting your customer meetings?
[seg_0020] Client (220.72-226.82): Late afternoon is generally better. If I miss the call, leave a simple callback message and I'll return it when I'm free.
[seg_0021] Advisor (227.22-236.68): Certainly. I'll keep any voicemail brief. Thank you for your time today, Adrian. I'll be in touch regarding the administrative follow-up.
[seg_0022] Client (237.08-242.60): Thanks, Rachel. That's fine. I'll keep an eye out for your call. Have a good afternoon.

call_intent.reasoning: The advisor made a specific product recommendation (Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund) tailored to the client's investment objectives (Advisory). Although the client subsequently placed a buy instruction for this fund, instructions following an advisor's recommendation of the same product fall under Advisory rather than Execution-Only. Additionally, service request details regarding routine contact preferences were updated (Enquiry).

Notice on Recommendations On Investment Products 30  
Documentation and Record Keeping 
 
35 The financial adviser shall make reasonable efforts to document the basis 
for the recommendation referred to in paragraph 36(b), and such documentation 
shall include the following: 
 
(a) the client’s statement of his investment objectives, financial situation 
and particular needs; 
 
(b) the financial adviser’s reasonable basis for making the 
recommendation to the client having regard to the information 
obtained from the client; and 
 
(c) the financial adviser’s assessment of the disadvantages of the 
investment product based on circumstances of the client. 
 
36 A financial adviser shall furnish to its client a document containing the 
following when making a recommendation in respect of an investment product to 
the client: 
(a) a summary of the information gathered by the financial adviser 
pursuant to paragraph 11; and 
 
(b) any recommendation made to the client by the financial adviser 
and the basis for the recommendation, 
 
and, where applicable, also furnish to its client a statement that the client does

PRIVATE BANKING SALES AND ADVISORY PRACTICES                                                                                                          FEBRUARY 2020 
_______________________________________________________________________________________ 
MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE  18 
5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES 
 
5.1 PBs should establish requirements for RMs to provide clients with adequate 
pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should 
communicate to clients, and agree with them,  the fees1 charged to them in a timely and 
transparent way. Any d eviations from agreed pricing arrangements should be clearly 
disclosed to clients on a timely basis, with their agreement or “no objection”  properly 
documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.  
 
5.2 Fee schedules – All PBs provide clients with standard fee schedules at the time of 
account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
